postData.contentHtml:
In a firm declaration regarding the burgeoning field of artificial intelligence, a prominent advisor to the Trump administration has placed the onus of AI safety squarely on the shoulders of the tech companies themselves. The message is clear and direct: if AI technology cannot be developed safely, companies should simply 'just stop.'

This assertive stance underscores a broader philosophy within the administration, which tends to view concerns surrounding AI's existential risks as largely 'overblown.' According to reports, President Trump has even characterized calls for a slowdown in AI development as a 'conspiracy' that would primarily serve the interests of rival nations, specifically China. This perspective suggests a prioritization of rapid innovation and competitive advantage, with the expectation that industry leaders will self-regulate and ensure responsible development.

The advisor's comments imply a preference for corporate accountability and self-governance over potentially stifling external regulations. The administration appears to trust that the private sector possesses the necessary expertise and ethical frameworks to navigate the complex challenges of AI development.

Social media reaction to this position has been mixed, registering as 'mostly positive, with some debate.' This indicates a divided public opinion, with some likely supporting the call for corporate responsibility and a streamlined approach to innovation, while others may advocate for stronger governmental oversight and regulatory frameworks to mitigate potential risks.

Ultimately, the Trump administration's message to the AI industry is unequivocal: innovate, but do so responsibly. The ball, it seems, is firmly in the court of the AI developers to ensure their creations are not only groundbreaking but also inherently safe.
postData.title: Trump Advisor: AI Safety is Tech Companies' Responsibility, 'Just Stop' if Unsafe
postData.summary: A top Trump administration AI advisor asserts that AI companies bear the sole responsibility for their technology's safety, even suggesting a halt in development if safety isn't guaranteed. This stance aligns with the White House's view that AI fears are 'overblown,' with President Trump reportedly dismissing calls for an AI slowdown as a 'conspiracy' benefiting China.
